hero.title: Couple Quiz for Teenagers
hero.description: You've been together for a few weeks, months, maybe more. And inevitably, the question comes up: is this for real, or just a nice chapter? This quiz won't solve everything — but it'll ask the real questions.

r1.title: Your relationship is still finding its way
r1.text: This isn't a verdict. But your answers show something's off — maybe communication isn't clicking yet, different expectations, or a relationship that's just starting. Take time to really talk, without phones, without the group chat.
r1.advice: Try having a real conversation, {{name1}} and {{name2}}, without your phones, without pressure. Ask yourselves: what do you really expect from each other?

r2.title: You have something, but it needs work
r2.text: There's a real foundation between {{name1}} and {{name2}}. Strong moments, a connection that exists. But some areas are still fuzzy. What matters is whether you both want to go for it.
r2.advice: Take a moment to talk about what's working between you, and what could improve. The key is making these conversations regular.

r3.title: Your couple has solid foundations
r3.text: {{name1}} and {{name2}}, you know each other, you trust each other, you see a future. It's not perfect (it never is) but it's solid.
r3.advice: Keep surprising each other and don't take anything for granted. Solid couples are those who keep nurturing their relationship.

r4.title: Your relationship really has what it takes to last
r4.text: {{name1}} and {{name2}}'s answers paint a picture of a couple that communicates, respects each other, plans ahead, and makes each other happy. That's rare, and it needs nurturing.
r4.advice: Enjoy every moment together. Relationships like yours don't happen by accident — they're built day after day.

seo.s1Title: Teen couple quiz: why asking these questions is already a good sign
seo.s1P1: When you're a teenager in a relationship, nobody really gives you a manual. Your parents have their opinion (often unsolicited), your friends too, and the internet drowns you in advice that doesn't really speak to you. Yet the question 'is our relationship actually solid?' always shows up eventually.
seo.s1P2: It's not a bad question. It's actually one of the best you can ask. Not because you're in trouble — but because questioning things together is one of the most mature things you can do in a relationship.
seo.s2Title: What does a solid relationship look like when you're a teen?
seo.s2P1: The short answer: it's not necessarily one that lasts 10 years. It's what people call a healthy relationship — one where you feel good, respected, free to be yourselves. A relationship that helps you grow rather than weighs you down.
seo.s2Sub1: Signs of a healthy teen relationship:
seo.s2L1: You can talk without judging each other
seo.s2L2: You each keep your own friends and interests
seo.s2L3: You're not afraid of the other's reaction when you say no
seo.s2L4: You make each other feel good, even in ordinary moments
seo.s2L5: You can argue and make up without deep scars
seo.s2Sub2: On the other hand, some warning signs:
seo.s2W1: You feel obligated to change for them
seo.s2W2: You're afraid of their reaction when you express a different opinion
seo.s2W3: You spend more time managing crises than having good moments
seo.s2W4: Your friends say they see you less since you've been together
seo.s2W5: You're exhausted after spending time with them
seo.s3Title: Can a teen relationship actually last?
seo.s3P1: Yes. And no. Both answers are honest. The reality is that most teen relationships don't last — not because they aren't genuine, but because you change fast at that age. Your tastes, ambitions, and personality evolve enormously between 15 and 20.
seo.s3P2: But some couples that form in adolescence last decades. It's not an urban legend. What sets them apart isn't luck — it's usually communication, mutual respect, and the ability to adapt together to changes.
seo.s4Title: Long distance as a teen: myth or reality?
seo.s4P1: It's one of the most common questions. College, moving, different schools... distance often comes sooner than you think. Managing a long-distance relationship can work. But it takes much more effort than a 'regular' relationship.
seo.s4P2: What really helps: regular video calls, shared plans to look forward to, clear communication about expectations, and total honesty about how you're experiencing the distance.
seo.s4Tip: If you know you'll be separated soon, talk about it now. Not dramatically — just an honest conversation about what you both want. It's 100 times healthier than waiting for it to happen.
seo.s5Title: Jealousy in teen relationships: normal or not?
seo.s5P1: A little jealousy is human. No one will tell you otherwise. But there's a huge difference between 'I felt a twinge of jealousy' and 'I check their phone / I make them cut off friends.'
seo.s5P2: Poorly managed jealousy is one of the leading causes of breakups and suffering in teen couples — and can quickly turn a relationship toxic. It often comes from a lack of confidence — not necessarily in the other person, but in yourself.
seo.s5Tip: Jealousy doesn't prove you care about the other person. It proves you're afraid of losing them. That's not the same thing. Working on that fear is what really changes things.
seo.s6Title: How to know if you're in love or just attached?
seo.s6P1: Love looks like this: you think about them and it makes you happy. You want them to thrive, even if it's not convenient for you. You want to share your life with this person, not just have someone by your side.
seo.s6P2: Attachment by habit or fear looks more like: you stay because you're afraid of being alone. You don't really see a future together, but breaking up seems too complicated.
seo.s7Title: Social media and relationships: managing without losing yourself
seo.s7P1: What your partner posts online isn't necessarily a threat. A like, a follow, a watched story — none of that says anything about their feelings for you. Projecting intentions onto it is exhausting for both of you.
seo.s7P2: Having clear rules about what you post together (or not), what goes on stories, how you talk about your relationship online — that's a useful conversation. Not to control each other, but to be aligned.
seo.s7Tip: If social media is regularly causing conflict in your relationship, ask yourself: is the problem really the app, or is it revealing a trust issue that exists elsewhere?
seo.s8Title: Teen breakup: how to actually recover
seo.s8P1: No false promises: a breakup hurts, even when you're the one who decided to leave. The stages of a breakup are well documented, and getting through them takes time — a relationship takes up space in your life.
seo.s8P2: What actually helps: don't try to erase them from your life too abruptly, talk to your friends, don't judge yourself for what you feel, give yourself time, and start doing things that make you happy again.
seo.faq1Q: How does the teen couple quiz work?
seo.faq1A: Create a session, share the code with your partner. You each answer 20 randomly selected questions from 80 on your own. Answers are only revealed at the end for an honest result.
seo.faq2Q: Is it really free with no registration?
seo.faq2A: Yes, completely free. No registration, no email, no account needed. Play directly from your browser.
seo.faq3Q: Can we play again with different questions?
seo.faq3A: Yes! Each session randomly picks 20 questions from 80. You can replay as many times as you want to discover new questions.
seo.faq4A: Sessions expire automatically after 30 minutes. No personal data is permanently stored.
